---
title: "Fit a BayesR Mixture Model (MCMC or stochastic EM)"
---

## Fit a BayesR Mixture Model (MCMC or stochastic EM) {.unnumbered}


### Description

BayesR (Erbe et al., 2012) places a four-component mixture prior on
allele effects: <em>zero</em>, <em>small</em>, <em>medium</em>, and
<em>large</em> effect classes with proportions <code>pi_vec</code> and class
variances proportional to <code>sigma2_ah</code>. Use <code>method = "mcmc"</code>
for full Bayesian posterior inference, or <code>method = "em"</code> for
fast stochastic-EM point estimates (Gaussian only) (Wang et al., 2015).



### Usage

<pre><code class='language-R'>run_bayesr(
  w,
  y,
  X = NULL,
  marker_type = c("auto", "snp", "multiallelic"),
  pi_vec = c(0.95, 0.02, 0.02, 0.01),
  sigma2_e_init,
  sigma2_ah = NULL,
  sigma2_vec = NULL,
  prior_params = NULL,
  mcmc_params = NULL,
  em_params = NULL,
  method = c("mcmc", "em"),
  response_type = c("gaussian", "binary"),
  fold_id = 0L,
  save_rds = FALSE,
  save_path = NULL,
  verbose = FALSE,
  map = NULL,
  windsize = NULL,
  windnum = NULL
)
</code></pre>


### Arguments

<table>
<tr><td style = "white-space: collapse; font-family: monospace; vertical-align: top"><code id="w">w</code></td>
<td>
Numeric design matrix (<code>n x p</code>). Typically the
<code>\$W_ah</code> element returned by <code>construct_wah_matrix</code>
or the <code>\$W</code> element returned by <code>construct_snp_matrix</code>.
</td></tr>
<tr><td style = "white-space: collapse; font-family: monospace; vertical-align: top"><code id="y">y</code></td>
<td>
Phenotype vector (length <code>n</code>). For binary traits use 0/1
coding.
</td></tr>
<tr><td style = "white-space: collapse; font-family: monospace; vertical-align: top"><code id="X">X</code></td>
<td>
Optional fixed-effects design matrix (<code>n x q</code>). When
supplied, the model is $y = X\alpha + W\beta + \mu + \epsilon$
with a flat prior on $\alpha$. Do <strong>not</strong> include a column
of ones for the intercept; $\mu$ is sampled separately.
</td></tr>
<tr><td style = "white-space: collapse; font-family: monospace; vertical-align: top"><code id="marker_type">marker_type</code></td>
<td>
One of <code>"auto"</code> (default), <code>"snp"</code>, or
<code>"multiallelic"</code>. <code>"auto"</code> resolves to
<code>"multiallelic"</code>. Selects the default prior for the BayesR
sampler — see <code>sigma2_ah</code>, <code>sigma2_e_init</code>,
<code>prior_params</code>. SNP path additionally rescales
<code>variance_class</code> by <code>ncol(w) / sum(apply(w, 2, var))</code>.
</td></tr>
<tr><td style = "white-space: collapse; font-family: monospace; vertical-align: top"><code id="pi_vec">pi_vec</code></td>
<td>
Initial mixture proportions for the four classes (zero,
small, medium, large). Must sum to 1. Default
<code>c(0.95, 0.02, 0.02, 0.01)</code>.
</td></tr>
<tr><td style = "white-space: collapse; font-family: monospace; vertical-align: top"><code id="sigma2_e_init">sigma2_e_init</code></td>
<td>
Initial residual variance. Default for
<code>"snp"</code>: <code>var(y) / 2</code>. <code>"multiallelic"</code>: required
(typically <code>var(y) * 0.5</code>; for binary use <code>1.0</code>).
</td></tr>
<tr><td style = "white-space: collapse; font-family: monospace; vertical-align: top"><code id="sigma2_ah">sigma2_ah</code></td>
<td>
Prior total genetic variance. Default for
<code>"snp"</code>: <code>var(y) / 4</code>. <code>"multiallelic"</code>: required
(typically <code>var(y) * 0.5</code>; for binary use <code>1.0</code>).
</td></tr>
<tr><td style = "white-space: collapse; font-family: monospace; vertical-align: top"><code id="sigma2_vec">sigma2_vec</code></td>
<td>
Optional explicit variance vector for EM; if
<code>NULL</code> it is derived from <code>sigma2_ah</code>, <code>pi_vec</code>, and
<code>prior_params\$variance_class</code>.
</td></tr>
<tr><td style = "white-space: collapse; font-family: monospace; vertical-align: top"><code id="prior_params">prior_params</code></td>
<td>
Optional named list overriding defaults. User-
supplied fields always win. Recognised: <code>a0_e</code>, <code>a0_g</code>,
<code>variance_class</code>. Defaults for <code>"snp"</code>:
<code>a0_e = -1</code>, <code>a0_g = 2</code>,
<code>variance_class = c(0, 0.0001, 0.001, 0.01)</code>. For
<code>"multiallelic"</code>: <code>a0_e = 10</code>, <code>a0_g = 10</code>,
<code>variance_class = c(0, 0.001, 0.01, 0.1)</code>. <code>b0_e</code> and
<code>b0_g</code> are computed internally.
</td></tr>
<tr><td style = "white-space: collapse; font-family: monospace; vertical-align: top"><code id="mcmc_params">mcmc_params</code></td>
<td>
Optional named list: <code>n_iter</code> (40000),
<code>n_burn</code> (20000), <code>n_thin</code> (10), <code>seed</code> (123).
</td></tr>
<tr><td style = "white-space: collapse; font-family: monospace; vertical-align: top"><code id="em_params">em_params</code></td>
<td>
Optional named list: <code>max_iter</code> (500), <code>tol</code>
(<code>1e-6</code>).
</td></tr>
<tr><td style = "white-space: collapse; font-family: monospace; vertical-align: top"><code id="method">method</code></td>
<td>
Either <code>"mcmc"</code> (default) or <code>"em"</code>.
</td></tr>
<tr><td style = "white-space: collapse; font-family: monospace; vertical-align: top"><code id="response_type">response_type</code></td>
<td>
<code>"gaussian"</code> (default) or <code>"binary"</code>.
Binary requires <code>method = "mcmc"</code>.
</td></tr>
<tr><td style = "white-space: collapse; font-family: monospace; vertical-align: top"><code id="fold_id">fold_id</code></td>
<td>
Integer label printed in progress messages; useful when
running CV loops.
</td></tr>
<tr><td style = "white-space: collapse; font-family: monospace; vertical-align: top"><code id="save_rds">save_rds</code></td>
<td>
If <code>TRUE</code> (default) the fit object is written to
disk as an RDS file. Set <code>FALSE</code> (default) for CV loops.
</td></tr>
<tr><td style = "white-space: collapse; font-family: monospace; vertical-align: top"><code id="save_path">save_path</code></td>
<td>
Optional explicit RDS path. If <code>NULL</code> (default),
defaults to <code>"results_bayesr.Rds"</code> in the current working
directory.
</td></tr>
<tr><td style = "white-space: collapse; font-family: monospace; vertical-align: top"><code id="verbose">verbose</code></td>
<td>
If <code>TRUE</code>, the Rust engine streams per-iteration
progress (start banner, Iter X/Y diagnostics, ESS / Geweke,
completion) to stderr. Default <code>FALSE</code> keeps the Rust side
silent. The brief R post-fit summary (model, runtime, $h^2$,
ESS, Geweke) prints regardless.
</td></tr>
<tr><td style = "white-space: collapse; font-family: monospace; vertical-align: top"><code id="map">map</code></td>
<td>
Optional GWAS map. Supplying <code>map</code> (together with
exactly one of <code>windsize</code> or <code>windnum</code>) computes per-allele
PIP, per-block PIP, and per-window WPPA from the posterior samples
and attaches them to the fit. For SNP markers, supply a data.frame
with columns <code>SNP</code>, <code>CHROM</code>, <code>POS</code> (one row per W
column). For multi-allelic (MH) markers, supply a data.frame with
columns <code>block_id</code>, <code>chr</code>, <code>start_pos</code>, <code>end_pos</code>
(one row per unique block_id in <code>attr(w, "block_id")</code>); this
matches the schema of <code>microhaplotype_coordinates.csv</code> from the
<code>maspipeline</code> tool. Marker type is auto-detected from
<code>attr(w, "block_id")</code>. <code>map = NULL</code> (default) skips the
GWAS branch and returns a fit object with no <code>pip</code>/<code>gwas</code>
fields.
</td></tr>
<tr><td style = "white-space: collapse; font-family: monospace; vertical-align: top"><code id="windsize">windsize</code></td>
<td>
Window size in base pairs for WPPA. Mutually exclusive
with <code>windnum</code>. Required when <code>map</code> is supplied unless
<code>windnum</code> is.
</td></tr>
<tr><td style = "white-space: collapse; font-family: monospace; vertical-align: top"><code id="windnum">windnum</code></td>
<td>
Number of consecutive markers (or MH blocks) per window
for WPPA. Mutually exclusive with <code>windsize</code>.
</td></tr>
</table>


### Details

<strong>Statistical model.</strong>
The base linear model for BayesR is:

<p style="text-align: center;"><code class="reqn">y = \mathbf{1}\mu + W\beta + \varepsilon, \quad
  \varepsilon \sim \mathcal{N}(0,\,\sigma_e^2 I)</code>


where $y$ is the phenotype vector, $\mu$ is the intercept,
$W$ is the marker design matrix (from
<code>construct_wah_matrix</code> for multi-allelic or
<code>construct_snp_matrix</code> for SNP markers), and $\beta$
is the allele-effect vector. When fixed effects are supplied via <code>X</code>:

<p style="text-align: center;">$y = \mathbf{1}\mu + X\alpha + W\beta + \varepsilon$


<strong>BayesR mixture prior.</strong>

<p style="text-align: center;"><code class="reqn">\beta_j \mid \pi,\,\sigma_\beta^2 \;\sim\;
  \pi_0\,\mathcal{N}(0,0)
  + \pi_1\,\mathcal{N}(0,\,c_1\sigma_\beta^2)
  + \pi_2\,\mathcal{N}(0,\,c_2\sigma_\beta^2)
  + \pi_3\,\mathcal{N}(0,\,c_3\sigma_\beta^2)</code>


where $(c_1,c_2,c_3)$ are the nonzero classes of
<code>variance_class</code> and $\pi$ is updated each MCMC iteration via
Dirichlet posterior. Residual: $\sigma_e^2 \sim \mathrm{InvGamma}(a_{0e},\,b_{0e})$.
Genetic base scale: $\sigma_g^2 \sim \mathrm{InvGamma}(a_{0g},\,b_{0g})$.

<strong>Algorithm choice.</strong> MCMC uses marginalised Gibbs sampling and
returns full posterior chains; recommended when posterior uncertainty,
ESS, or Geweke diagnostics are needed. EM is much faster but yields no
uncertainty quantification and does not support <code>response_type =
"binary"</code>.

<strong>Auto-save.</strong> By default the returned fit is also saved to
<code>results_bayesr.Rds</code> in <code>getwd()</code>. Set <code>save_rds = FALSE</code>
(or pass an explicit <code>save_path</code>) when running cross-validation
loops to avoid overwriting earlier folds.

<strong>Three usage scenarios.</strong> The same <code>run_bayesr()</code> +
<code>summary()</code> + <code>predict()</code> pipeline supports:


<ul>
<li> <em>Full-data fit:</em> train on all data; <code>predict(fit)</code>
returns in-sample metrics.

</li>
<li> <em>Train-test split:</em> train on a subset; evaluate via
<code>predict(fit, W_test, y_test)</code>.

</li>
<li> <em>k-fold CV:</em> the user loops over folds, calling
<code>run_bayesr()</code> with <code>save_rds = FALSE</code> and <code>fold_id =
    k</code>, then <code>predict()</code> on each held-out fold.

</li></ul>



### Value

An object of class <code>c("masbayes_bayesr", "masbayes")</code> — a
list with the following key fields:


<dl>
<dt><code>beta_hat, mu_hat, sigma2_e_hat</code></dt><dd>Posterior point
estimates.
</dd>
<dt><code>beta_samples, gamma_samples, pi_samples,
    sigma2_e_samples, sigma2_small_samples, sigma2_medium_samples,
    sigma2_large_samples, mu_samples</code></dt><dd>Posterior chains (single-row
matrices for EM).
</dd>
<dt><code>GEBV / pred_train</code></dt><dd>Training genomic estimated breeding
values. For binary traits this is on the <em>liability</em> scale.
</dd>
<dt><code>prob_train</code></dt><dd>Binary only: training-set predicted
probabilities <code>P(y = 1) = pnorm(pred_train)</code> (probit
inverse link from Albert-Chib augmentation).
</dd>
<dt><code>h2, sigma2_g, sigma2_e</code></dt><dd>Heritability and variance
components.
</dd>
<dt><code>runtime</code></dt><dd>Elapsed seconds.
</dd>
<dt><code>training_metrics</code></dt><dd><code>R2</code>, <code>RMSE</code>,
<code>accuracy</code> (or <code>AUC</code> for binary), <code>bias</code>. For
binary, all metrics are on the observed (probability) scale —
<code>bias</code> is the calibration slope (1.0 = perfectly
calibrated) and <code>RMSE\^2</code> approximates the Brier score.
AUC is rank-invariant so unaffected.
</dd>
<dt><code>diagnostics</code></dt><dd>ESS and Geweke Z for key parameters
(MCMC only).
</dd>
<dt><code>variance_components</code></dt><dd>Posterior mean and 95% CI for
each class plus the mixture proportions <code>pi</code>.
</dd>
<dt><code>rds_path</code></dt><dd>Path of the saved RDS file, or <code>NULL</code>
when <code>save_rds = FALSE</code>.
</dd>
<dt><code>pip</code></dt><dd>(GWAS only, since v0.5.0) Per-allele posterior
inclusion probability, length <code>ncol(w)</code>. Computed as
<code>colMeans(gamma_samples != 0)</code>. <code>NULL</code> unless <code>map</code>
was supplied.
</dd>
<dt><code>pip_block</code></dt><dd>(GWAS only) Per-block PIP, length
<code>nrow(map)</code>. For SNP markers, identical to <code>pip</code>. For
multi-allelic markers, a block is &quot;active&quot; in a posterior sample
if at least one of its alleles has <code>gamma != 0</code>. <code>NULL</code>
unless <code>map</code> was supplied.
</dd>
<dt><code>gwas</code></dt><dd>(GWAS only) Data frame with columns <code>Wind</code>,
<code>Chr</code>, <code>N</code>, <code>Start</code>, <code>End</code>, <code>WPPA</code>. Each
row is one physical window; <code>WPPA</code> is the window posterior
probability of association, i.e. the fraction of posterior samples
in which at least one marker / block in the window has non-zero
effect.
</dd>
<dt><code>gwas_meta</code></dt><dd>(GWAS only) List capturing the call:
<code>windsize</code>, <code>windnum</code>, <code>midpoint_convention</code>,
<code>marker_type</code>, <code>n_windows</code>.
</dd>
</dl>



### GWAS

Supplying a <code>map</code> together with exactly one of <code>windsize</code> or
<code>windnum</code> turns <code>run_bayesr()</code> into a one-shot GWAS engine
alongside genomic prediction. The Rust kernel is untouched; PIP and
WPPA are derived from the existing <code>gamma_samples</code> matrix.

<strong>Map schema.</strong> For <strong>SNP</strong> markers, <code>map</code> is a
<code>data.frame</code> with columns <code>SNP</code> (character), <code>CHROM</code>
(integer), <code>POS</code> (integer), one row per W column.
For <strong>multi-allelic (MH)</strong> markers, <code>map</code> has columns
<code>block_id</code> (character), <code>chr</code> (integer), <code>start_pos</code>
(integer), <code>end_pos</code> (integer), one row per unique block_id in
<code>attr(w, "block_id")</code>. The MH schema matches the
<code>microhaplotype_coordinates.csv</code> produced by the
<code>maspipeline</code> tool, so production pipelines can pass it through
without translation.

<strong>Windows.</strong> <code>windsize</code> (bp) closes a window when the next
marker's position exceeds the window start by <code>windsize</code>.
<code>windnum</code> groups <code>windnum</code> consecutive markers / blocks per
window. Windows never cross chromosome boundaries.

<strong>Constraints.</strong> GWAS requires <code>method = "mcmc"</code> (EM has no
posterior samples). <code>run_bayesa</code> accepts the same
arguments for API symmetry but errors out (BayesA has no zero-effect
mixture mass, so PIP / WPPA are ill-defined). <code>map = NULL</code>
(default) skips the GWAS branch entirely.



### References

Erbe, M., Hayes, B. J., Matukumalli, L. K., Goswami, S., Bowman, P. J.,
Reich, C. M., Mason, B. A., \&amp; Goddard, M. E. (2012). Improving
accuracy of genomic predictions within and between dairy cattle
breeds with imputed high-density single nucleotide polymorphism
panels. <em>Journal of Dairy Science</em>, 95(7), 4114-4129.
[doi:10.3168/jds.2011-5019](https://doi.org/10.3168/jds.2011-5019)

Wang, T., Chen, YP. P., \&amp; Goddard, M. E. (2015).
A computationally efficient algorithm for genomic prediction using
a Bayesian model. <em>Genet Sel Evol</em>, 47(34).
[doi:10.1186/s12711-014-0082-4](https://doi.org/10.1186/s12711-014-0082-4)

### Examples
```{r, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE, eval=FALSE}
library("masbayes")

d <- load_data("small")
mcmc <- list(n_iter = 1000L, n_burn = 500L, n_thin = 5L, seed = 123L)

# ---- (A) SNP path -----------------------------------------------------
# Pair `encoding = "zscore"` on the matrix builder with
# `marker_type = "snp"` on the fitter for the alternative biallelic-SNP
# convention.
snp_train <- construct_snp_matrix(d$snp[d$train_idx, ], encoding = "zscore")
W_train   <- snp_train$W
y_train   <- d$pheno$y_cont_qtl_snp[d$train_idx]
X_train   <- model.matrix(~ sex - 1, data = d$pheno[d$train_idx, ])

fit_snp <- run_bayesr(
  w             = W_train,
  y             = y_train,
  X             = X_train,
  marker_type   = "snp",
  sigma2_e_init = var(y_train) * 0.5,
  sigma2_ah     = var(y_train) * 0.5,
  mcmc_params   = mcmc,
  save_rds      = FALSE
)
summary(fit_snp)

# ---- (B) Microhaplotype path -----------------------------------------
# d$mh is consumable directly by construct_wah_matrix via attr("block_id").
# d$allele_freq is the frequency table required for the training call.
bid    <- attr(d$mh, "block_id")
hap_tr <- d$mh[d$train_idx, ]
W_mh   <- construct_wah_matrix(hap_tr, bid, d$allele_freq)$W_ah
y_mh   <- d$pheno$y_cont_qtl_mh[d$train_idx]

# ---- (C) GWAS (BayesR-only) ------------------------------------------
# Supply `map` together with `windsize` (bp) or `windnum` (markers per
# window) to compute per-allele PIP, per-block PIP, and per-window WPPA.
# Schema for SNP map: SNP / CHROM / POS (one row per W column).
# The map's row order does not need to be pre-sorted.
map_snp <- data.frame(
  SNP   = paste0("M", seq_len(ncol(W_train))),
  CHROM = rep(seq_len(4L), each = ncol(W_train) %/% 4L),
  POS   = rep(seq(1e6, by = 1e5,
                  length.out = ncol(W_train) %/% 4L), 4L)
)
fit_gwas <- run_bayesr(
  w             = W_train,
  y             = y_train,
  marker_type   = "snp",
  sigma2_e_init = var(y_train) * 0.5,
  sigma2_ah     = var(y_train) * 0.5,
  mcmc_params   = mcmc,
  save_rds      = FALSE,
  map           = map_snp,
  windsize      = 5e5
)
head(fit_gwas$gwas[order(-fit_gwas$gwas$WPPA), ], 5)

fit_mh <- run_bayesr(
  w             = W_mh,
  y             = y_mh,
  X             = X_train,
  sigma2_e_init = var(y_mh) * 0.5,
  sigma2_ah     = var(y_mh) * 0.5,
  mcmc_params   = mcmc,
  save_rds      = FALSE
)
summary(fit_mh)




```
